Graph of Fitted Densities at Chosen Covariate Values

Source: R/plot_model.R
plot_density.Rd

Selects the graph of the density, or the mass function, that the fit gives at each row of a data frame of covariate values. With over, each density is drawn vertically at its position on the horizontal axis, over the observed data; without it, the densities are overlaid and coloured by row.

Usage

plot_density(at, over = NULL, n_grid = 200, scale = 0.9, legend = TRUE)

Arguments

at

A data frame of covariate values, one fitted distribution per row.

over

NULL, or the name of a numeric covariate of at that gives the position of each density on the horizontal axis.

n_grid

The number of points of the response grid of a continuous family.

scale

With over, the width of the widest density as a fraction of the smallest gap between positions (of 15 per cent of the range of the covariate for a single row).

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotDensity object, inheriting from model_plot.

Details

Each row of at is completed with the other covariates of the model, held at their median (numeric) or first level (factor), and the random effects are set to zero. The response range of each row runs from the quantile 0.001 to the quantile 0.999 of its fitted distribution. For a continuous family the density is evaluated on n_grid points of that range. For a discrete family the mass is drawn at the integers from the smallest to the largest of those quantiles over the rows, as bars or, beside the data, as horizontal segments. The graph is not available for a multivariate family.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_quantiles()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(150))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(150, sd = exp(-1 + dd$x))
fit <- statmod(y ~ x | sigma ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_density(at = data.frame(x = c(0.1, 0.5,
                                                                  0.9)),
                                           over = "x"), data = dd)
